subject: Tower Floor Four
text: In Tower Floor Four, follow Zelda around the burning rubble in the middle of the room and proceed through the door after she opens it.

evidence.quote:
Follow Zelda to the right, around the burning rubble in the middle of the room.
Go through the door after Zelda opens it.

subject: Tower Exterior
text: Follow Zelda down Tower Exterior and go through the door at the bottom after she opens it.

evidence.quote:
Keep following Zelda down the tower.  When she opens the door at the bottom, go
through it.

subject: Tower Floor Three Stalfos
text: In Tower Floor Three, Zelda is trapped behind a pillar of flame in the middle of the room and two Stalfos appear that must be defeated to progress.

evidence.quote:
Keep near Zelda in this room, and when she reaches the middle of the room
she'll be trapped behind a pillar of flame.  Two Stalfos will appear, and
you've got to defeat them to progress.

subject: Tower Floor Three Stalfos
text: Casting Nayru's Love and attacking with the Biggoron Sword allows you to quickly defeat the two Stalfos in Tower Floor Three to free Zelda.

evidence.quote:
You don't have time to play it
carefully, so use Nayru's Love and the Biggoron Sword and just go kamikaze on
the Stalfos.  Once they are both dead, Zelda will be freed.

subject: Tower Floor Two
text: In Tower Floor Two, follow Zelda through the burning rubble and through the door she opens, down the stairs, and through the door on the left at the bottom.

evidence.quote:
Follow Zelda through the burning rubble, and when she reaches the door she'll
open it.  Go through the door here, and keep following Zelda down the stairs.
At the bottom, Zelda will open the door on the left.  Go through it.

subject: Keep Bridge Redead
text: A Redead is positioned on the bridge in the Keep of Ganon's Castle, which can be run past or killed with the Biggoron Sword.

evidence.quote:
Run along to the end of the bridge.  Run past the Redead (whose sole purpose
seems to be to waste whatever precious seconds you may have remaining), or kill
it with the Biggoron Sword.

subject: Keep Bridge
text: At the other end of the bridge in the Keep, Zelda opens the door leading up the stairs to the final door to escape the tower.

evidence.quote:
At the other end of the bridge, Zelda will open
the door.  Go through it and up the stairs on the other side, and wait for
Zelda to open the final door to escape the tower.

subject: Ganon
text: After Ganondorf transforms into Ganon among the tower ruins, Link lacks access to the Master Sword at first, but Navi is available to Z-Target Ganon.

evidence.quote:
After a cutscene, run forward towards the ruins of the tower, where Ganondorf
will emerge.  Except now he has been transformed into the evil demon Ganon....At the start of the fight you won't have access to the Master Sword....For this
ultimate showdown, Navi will be available for you to Z-Target Ganon, unlike in
the previous fight against him.

subject: Ganon
text: Ganon's weakspot is his tail, which can be struck with a Jump Attack using the Biggoron Sword or Megaton Hammer after performing side dodges to get behind him.

evidence.quote:
Like all evil demons of the underworld, Ganon's weakspot is his tail.  In his
first phase, you'll have to Z-Target Ganon and then begin performing side
dodges (hold right or left and press A) to speed around behind Ganon.  When you
get behind him, do a Jump Attack with the Biggoron Sword or Megaton Hammer to
deal a hefty amount of damage to Ganon.

subject: Master Sword
text: Damaging Ganon's tail repeatedly lowers the perimeter flames around the arena, allowing Link to run to Zelda and reclaim the Master Sword.

evidence.quote:
Repeat this method until a cutscene shows the flames around the perimeter of
the arena lowering.  Run over to Zelda and retake the Master Sword when this
happens.

subject: Ganon
text: In the final phase, get behind Ganon by shooting his face with a Light Arrow or rolling between his legs, attack his tail, and strike the final blow with the Master Sword.

evidence.quote:
You have two options: shoot him in the face with a Light Arrow, or
release your Z-Target and roll between his legs.  Whichever path you choose,
once you are on his backside, Z-Target him and perform a Jump Attack on his
tail....Only the Master Sword can defeat Ganon.  After a cutscene, you will be
prompted to attack Ganondorf while he is being held in place by Zelda's magic.
Do this, and the game is over.

subject: Main Adventure Progression
text: The game's standard progression chart outlines 35 main steps from obtaining the Kokiri Sword and Deku Shield to defeating Ganon.

evidence.quote:
This is the Walkthrough for people who don't want to be told exactly what
to do and where to go, but is instead a general outline of the game's standard
and preferred progression chart...35. Defeat Ganon.

subject: Happy Mask Salesman Sidequest
text: The Happy Mask Salesman sidequest is available to Young Link at the Happy Mask Shop in Hyrule Castle Market after opening the gate to Death Mountain Trail.

evidence.quote:
The Happy Mask Salesman Sidequest is the only Sidequest available to Young
Link.  The sidequest begins at the Happy Mask Shop in Hyrule Castle Market, at
any time after the opening the gate to Death Mountain Trail.

subject: Mask of Truth
text: Completing the Happy Mask Salesman sidequest awards the Mask of Truth, which allows reading hints from Gossip Stones across Hyrule.

evidence.quote:
The Happy Mask Salesman Sidequest ultimately nets you the Mask of Truth, which
lets you get hints from the Gossip Stones that dot Hyrule.

subject: Deku Stick and Deku Nut upgrades
text: Capacity upgrades for Deku Sticks and Deku Nuts are obtained in the Forest Stage in connection with the Happy Mask Salesman sidequest.

evidence.quote:
The only thing you really get out of this sidequest which
is worth mentioning is a Deku Stick and Deku Nut capacity upgrade, both of
which are obtained in the Forest Stage

subject: Keaton Mask
text: The Keaton Mask is borrowed for 10 Rupees and sold for 15 Rupees to the guard near the gate to Death Mountain Trail in Kakariko Village.

evidence.quote:
Sold To: Guard near the gate to Death Mountain Trail in Kakariko Village.
Borrow Price: 10 Rupees
Sell Price: 15 Rupees

subject: Skull Mask
text: The Skull Mask is borrowed for 15 Rupees and sold for 10 Rupees to the lone Skullkid in southwest Lost Woods.

evidence.quote:
Sold To: The Lone Skullkid in southwest Lost Woods.
Borrow Price: 15 Rupees
Sell Price: 10 Rupees

subject: Skull Mask
text: The Skull Mask allows access to the Deku Stick capacity upgrade in the Forest Stage.

evidence.quote:
The
Skull Mask also lets you access the Deku Stick capacity upgrade in the Forest
Stage.

subject: Spooky Mask
text: The Spooky Mask is borrowed for 30 Rupees and sold for 30 Rupees to Dampe's Fanboy in Kakariko Graveyard during the day.

evidence.quote:
Sold To: Dampe's Fanboy in the Kakariko Graveyard (daytime only)
Borrow Price: 30 Rupees
Sell Price: 30 Rupees

subject: Bunny Hood
text: The Bunny Hood is borrowed for 50 Rupees and sold for 500 Rupees to the Running Man in Hyrule Field after Jabu-Jabu's Belly is finished.

evidence.quote:
Sold To: The Running Man in Hyrule Field (only after Jabu-Jabu's Belly is
finished)
Borrow Price: 50 Rupees
Sell Price: 500 Rupees

subject: Bunny Hood Sale
text: Without the Giant's Wallet, Link will only receive 99 or 200 Rupees from the 500 Rupees the Running Man pays for the Bunny Hood.

evidence.quote:
Sell Price: 500 Rupees...if you don't have the Giant's Wallet then you'll only get 99 or 200 out of that
five hundred.

subject: Mask of Truth
text: The Mask of Truth can only be worn by Young Link to get hints from Gossip Stones, and can be used in the Forest Stage to earn a Deku Nut capacity upgrade.

evidence.quote:
The Mask of Truth, the best of the available masks, lets you use the Gossip
Stones around Hyrule to receive hints.  Which would be cool, except only Young
Link can wear the Mask of Truth...The Mask of Truth can also be used in the
Forest Stage to earn a Deku Nut capacity upgrade.

subject: Goron Mask
text: Wearing the Goron Mask causes Gorons to mistake Link for an actual Goron, deplore how small and weak he is, and insist he eat something.

evidence.quote:
When worn, this Masks makes those lovably foolish Gorons mistake you for an
actual Goron, who will deplore about what a small, weak Goron you are, and
insist you eat something.

subject: Zora Mask
text: Speaking to Zoras while wearing the Zora Mask causes them to treat Link sarcastically.

evidence.quote:
If you speak to Zoras while wearing this mask, they will sarcastically treat
you the way you'd expect a little kid running around in a mask to be treated.

subject: Gerudo Mask
text: The Gerudo Mask does not fool any of the Gerudos.

evidence.quote:
If you thought this mask would actually fool any of the Gerudos, then go jump
off a cliff.

subject: Epona's Song
text: Speaking with Malon in the pasture of Lon Lon Ranch as Young Link until she mentions her mother and playing the Ocarina teaches Epona's Song, which tames Epona and yields free milk from any cow.

evidence.quote:
Head for
Lon Lon Ranch during the daytime, and head for the middle of the pasture.
Speak with Malon until she mentions her mother, then pull out your Ocarina
(Fairy Ocarina, Ocarina of Time, it doesn't matter which).  Malon will then
teach you Epona's Song, which tames Epona and also makes any Cow in the game
give you a free bottle of Lon Lon Milk.

subject: Ingo Horse Rental
text: Speaking with Ingo at the rear pasture as Adult Link allows you to ride a horse for ten rupees.

evidence.quote:
Run to the pasture in the rear of the ranch, and speak with Ingo.
After a lengthy speech about how great Ganondorf is, Ingo will offer to let you
ride a horse for ten rupees.

subject: Epona
text: Playing Epona's Song inside the pasture causes Epona to appear and run toward Link.

evidence.quote:
Ignore the horse that Ingo offers you, and play Epona's Song.  Epona will
appear and run towards you.

subject: Ingo's First Race
text: Speaking to Ingo while riding Epona prompts a horse race for fifty rupees, which can be won by using two or three carrots to pass him on the inside rail of a corner and blocking him.

evidence.quote:
speak to Ingo while riding Epona and he will
challenge you to a race for fifty rupees....In the first race against Ingo, he goes fairly slowly, and
takes the corners very wide.  Stay close behind him until he gets near a
corner, then quickly hug the inside rail and burn two or three carrots to shoot
in front of him.  At this point, just carefully steer yourself to stay directly
in front Ingo, preventing him from getting in front of you.

subject: Ingo's Second Race
text: Winning the first race causes Ingo to bet Epona on a rematch where Link can burn two or three carrots on the first turn to pass and block him.

evidence.quote:
After you win the first race, Ingo will have a meltdown and frantically bet
Epona on a rematch.  Agree.  This time, Ingo will cheat and leave the starting
gate a second before the clock goes off.  Even though he now goes slightly
faster and cheats at the start, the race is still identical, and he still takes
turns incredibly wide.  Wait for the first turn in the track, and burn two or
three carrots to shoot in front of him while he takes the wide corner.
